      <title>Isak completes Liverpool’s comeback win as Brentford finish with nine</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/17/brentford-liverpool-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>If this truly was the turning point for Liverpool’s spluttering forwards then they will owe a big debt of gratitude to Yehor Yarmolyuk. Brentford were 1-0 up when their midfielder saw red for a head-butt on Jérémy Jacquet just before half-time and, while Andoni Iraola will hope that surviving one of the toughest tests the Premier League has to offer is a sign his methods are starting to take hold, the Spaniard will know it was very different contest once his side had a numerical advantage to exploit.</p><p>Brentford, whose unbeaten start to the season is over, raged at the officiating. They finished with nine men after losing Vitaly Janelt late on. John Brooks walked off to boos at full-time, although in truth Keith Andrews’ side only had themselves to blame. They pressed the self-destruct button when they had Liverpool on the ropes. Yarmolyuk was foolish and Liverpool punished him.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/17/brentford-liverpool-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Haaland helps extend record start for Maresca as Manchester City defeat Ipswich</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/17/manchester-city-ipswich-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>There have been few winners in Manchester City’s guilty verdict, except highly paid lawyers and the inflatable fruit industry. The fans have suffered, being forced to question everything they have been told, while being labelled “cheats” but they were able to forget the cacophony of noise around the club as Enzo Maresca became the first manager in history to win his first seven games in charge of a team.</p><p>Ipswich were the latest victims but they put up a fight in City’s first home Premier League game since being found to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/25/manchester-city-found-guilty-of-breaking-premier-leagues-financial-fair-play-rules">have breached financial rules</a>. Defiance has fortified the majority of the City fanbase, who were able to see local boy Phil Foden instigate the triumph with a kiss of the badge, before an emblem of their wealth, Erling Haaland, secured the points to move six clear of the nearest challengers with a clinical double, albeit with a few scares between.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/17/manchester-city-ipswich-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Pressure on Arbeloa lifted after Alex Iwobi sinks Hull for Fulham’s first win</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/17/fulham-hull-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p></p><p>After such a dominant performance against a team so blunt going forward, it almost felt inevitable that Álvaro Arbeloa was going to be denied his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach in similar fashion as the weeks and games before. After all their chances and possession, Craven Cottage should not have been a place of nerves when Mohamed Belloumi lined up a free-kick as three minutes of stoppage time were shown.</p><p>When the Hull winger blazed that free-kick over the bar – the closest Hull had come to scoring throughout the second half – the tension was released that little bit more. Despite Ryan Sessegnon’s late red card, the full-time whistle brought a first victory of the season, courtesy of Alex Iwobi’s first-half strike, and a release from the burden of being the Premier League’s basement club.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/17/fulham-hull-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p></p><p>Chelsea have returned from the international break with a spirit, authority and resilience that augurs well for Xabi Alonso. Their troubles at Everton, not a happy hunting ground in recent years, were confined to the seven minutes Emi Martínez needed treatment for a head injury as Pedro Neto’s double delivered a deserved victory in the Merseyside sunshine.</p><p>The Argentina goalkeeper was taken to hospital for tests after an accidental collision with Jarrad Branthwaite left him with suspected concussion. “When he left the stadium he was conscious,” Alonso said. “Hopefully it is not too bad but we need to wait.” A first Premier League clean sheet since January, and a second successive win since losing at Brentford before the Nations League break, were otherwise secured with a minimum of fuss in a commanding second-half performance.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/17/everton-chelsea-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment</p><p>The manner of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/11/liverpool-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report">Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool</a> was an article of both vindication and vilification. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums.       <description><p>What had been billed as a day of reckoning for the Premier League champions turned into a Sunday afternoon stroll</p><p>Anfield welcomed Manchester City to their new reality, a sullied place where every touch is accompanied by cries of “cheat”, any favourable decision is considered proof of further conspiracy and every victory hollow. The only body of irrefutable evidence in City’s favour <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/29/manchester-city-found-guilty-all-premier-league-charges-rule-breaches">since the guilty verdicts landed</a> is that Enzo Maresca’s league leaders appear immune to prosecution and persecution.</p><p>That may well change depending on the outcome of City’s appeal and any punishment that eventually arises, likewise the merits and value of a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/11/liverpool-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report">commanding 3-0 win</a> on Liverpool soil.
